#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
  done
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

# Hybrid simulator per-host configuration.
#
# This file is the TEMPLATE (committed). On first `source ./setup.sh`,
# it is copied to ./config.env (gitignored). Edit ./config.env to point
# at the toolchain on your host; never commit your local edits.
#
# Both setup.sh and the test harness scripts load ./config.env at
# startup, so an exported value in your shell takes precedence; this
# file fills in the gaps when something runs without prior `source`.

# Andes RISC-V GCC + libgloss_vh toolchain root (rv64). Must contain
# bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}.
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d

# The rv32 toolchain root (separate install), for building rv32 runtime/fixtures.
# Must contain bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-{gcc,ar,...}. Leave unset if you only
# target rv64; rv32 runtime/fixture builds are skipped without it.
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds32le-elf-newlib-v5d

# Directory holding the externally-built qemu-system-riscv32 AND -riscv64.
# This project no longer builds QEMU; you build it yourself and point here.
# setup.sh validates both binaries exist and exports VSIM_QEMU (rv64) +
# VSIM_QEMU32 (rv32) from this.
QEMU_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/build/qemu

# Directory holding the externally-built vsim sim_* binaries. This project no
# longer nests vsim as a submodule; you build it in your own vsim checkout (its
# build_vsim.sh) and point here. setup.sh exports VSIM_BIN_DIR from this, and the
# driver discovers cycle engines by scanning it (mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR).
VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build
---MAKEFILE---
# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so  -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotloops.so        -- hot inner-loop detector (developer profiling tool)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotloops.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

# hotloops is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not HYBRID_INCLUDE.
libhotloops.so: hotloops.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotloops.c $(LIBS)

clean:
	rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotloops.so

6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the vsim->QEMU2 handback was removed -- the run ends at the vsim drain).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	
14	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
15	
16	## Build Commands
17	
18	```sh
19	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin)
20	source ./setup.sh
21	
22	# Build individual components
23	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
24	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
25	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree)
26	
27	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
28	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
29	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
30	
31	# Clean
32	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|all]
33	```
34

36	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
37	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
38	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`

42	## Running Tests
43	
44	```sh
45	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
46	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
47	
48	# Run with specific options
49	JOBS=4 MODE=csr bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, CSR-mode only
50	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
51	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
52	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
53	
54	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
55	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
56	# To run ctest directly after build:
57	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
58	```
59	
60	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
61	
62	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
63	
64	**Manual plugin tests**: `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` are QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests. They are run manually during plugin development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one leg, asserts on stdout).
65	
66	## Architecture
67	
68	### Two-Phase Handoff
69	
70	```
71	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
72	```
73	
74	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
75	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
76	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
77	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg (gdbstub P-packet restore into a freshly spawned QEMU) was removed entirely.
78	
79	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are not restored anywhere -- they remain in the struct as the drained record only. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
80	
81	### Trigger Modes
82	
83	- **CSR mode** (default): Pattern-matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (entry) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
84	- **PC mode**: ELF symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed.
85	
86	Both modes coexist in the fixtures. `TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc` selects at runtime.
87	
88	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
89	
90	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
91	
92	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.
93	
94	### V-State Transport
95	
96	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a fixed scratch region
97	(`kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` on `-M andes_ae350`) in the shared mmap. vsim drives
98	the transfer via the Debug Module **Program Buffer** while the hart is halted, so
99	benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
100	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
101	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
102	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
103	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
104	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
105	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
106	
107	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
108	the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
109	compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
110	runtime vlenb.
111	
112	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
113	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
114	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
115	
116	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
117	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
118	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
119	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
120	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
121	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
122	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
123	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
124	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
125	
126	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
127	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
128	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
129	
130	### Test Fixtures
131	
132	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
133	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
134	the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Two fixture families:
135	
136	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
137	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
138	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
139	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | linked against vsim-demo C runtime. Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
140	
141	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
142	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
143	
144	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`. C-level fixtures link `runtime/{crt0.S, trap.S, handler.c}` plus the Andes toolchain's `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting-backed libgloss), using `rt_c.ld`. V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. **Phase-2 rule:** the span between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()` runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall (no `printf`, `fopen`, semihosting ebreak, etc.) -- vsim does not implement semihosting, so any libgloss-routed call inside the ROI traps. Phase 1 prints via standard newlib stdio (QEMU1 is launched with `-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`); the hybrid run ends at the vsim drain, so nothing after `exit_vsim()` executes.
145	
146	### vsim CMake Structure
147	
148	vsim lives entirely in `verilator/`. Key CMake options:
149	- `VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID` (default OFF) - enables e2e CTest registration
150	- `VSIM_CONFIG_FILE` - CPU YAML (default `config.yaml`)
151	- `VSIM_NO_VERILATOR` - skip Verilator build (assume prebuilt)
152	
153	The hybrid orchestration layer (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`) is header-only and depends only on C++20 standard library + the shared ABI header. SystemC/Verilator are not required for hybrid unit tests.
154	
155	Hybrid unit tests (`tests/hybrid/`) use [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest). They are registered in `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` and run via `ctest`. The `recording_bus.hpp` pattern provides a duck-typed test double for the DMI bus without requiring virtual interfaces.
156	
157	## Key Files
158	
159	| File | Purpose |
160	|------|---------|
161	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
162	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
163	| `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` | Phase dispatcher |
164	| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
165	| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | DMI state capture |
166	| `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` | V register transport via scratch region |
167	| `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` | CTest registration for all e2e fixtures |
168	| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
169	| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |

# Hybrid Simulator User Guide

Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
not study its internals. After this guide you can:

1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
3. Pick a switching mode (marker or PC) and run one handoff end-to-end
   with a concrete worked example.

For internals, read `docs/archive/hybrid_plan.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.

---

## 0. The one-paragraph mental model

QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT or PC)
hands control between them. One run is two legs:

```
   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
```

The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
mode".

---

## 0.5 Quick start with `./andesim`

`./andesim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
self-builds on first use). It drives `run` itself, orchestrating QEMU and
vsim directly; building is done by `scripts/build_all.sh` (which delegates to
`setup.sh`, `scripts/build_*.sh`). Sections 1-7 document those underlying
scripts (`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) for when you need to bypass
the driver.

Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:

```sh
bash scripts/build_all.sh                             # qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
./andesim list engines                                # discover the built engines
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one marker-mode handoff
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                          # the hybrid e2e suite (or scripts/test_all.sh for unit+contract+e2e)
```

Expected last line of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`:

```
summary: marker <N>p/0f/<S>s  pc <N>p/0f/<S>s  neg <N>p/0f/0s  total <N> passed, 0 failed, <S> skipped
```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `./andesim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
| `bash scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]`               | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `plugin`, `fixtures`, `runtime` (qemu and vsim are external prebuilt binaries, not built here). |
| `./andesim doctor`                                             | Read-only environment health check: artifacts, submodules, toolchain, runtime, discovered engines, and `/dev/shm` mmap tiers (with WSL2 advice). |
| `./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff and REQUIRES `--trigger marker|pc` to delimit the ROI; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the hybrid e2e suite directly (qemu+vsim round-trips). |
| `bash scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit\|contract\|e2e]`     | Run the full test surface: C++ unit tests + driver contracts + the e2e suite. |

Run `./andesim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
`ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal developer-only flags and the `list fixtures`
target). The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andesim`
(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).

---

## 1. Build and environment setup

### 1.1 Host prerequisites

Install these on the host once:

| Package          | Notes                                                |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
| `python3`        | orchestrator, plugin tests                           |
| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
| `pkg-config`     | plugin build (glib-2.0)                              |
| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
| QEMU             | prebuilt external binary; set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (not built here) |
| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |

The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.

### 1.2 Clone with submodules

```sh
git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
cd hybrid_sim
```

If you forgot `--recursive`:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Submodules under this repo:

| Path             | What it is                                          |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `include/`     | the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): `hybrid_state_v1` wire contract under `include/hybrid/` |

vsim is no longer a submodule -- it is a prebuilt **external** binary, like QEMU.
Build it in your own vsim (`hybrid_vsim`) checkout and point `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
(`config.env`) at its `build/` dir; see 1.3.

### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)

The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).

On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
`config.env`:

```sh
# config.env
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds32le-elf-newlib-v5d

The variables today:

| Variable            | What it points at                                                  |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`  | rv64 toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`| rv32 toolchain root (a *separate* install), for building the rv32 runtime + fixtures. `bin/` must contain `riscv32-unknown-elf-{gcc,ar,...}`. Optional: leave unset if you only target rv64 (rv32 builds are skipped). |
| `QEMU_BIN_DIR`      | External prebuilt QEMU build dir holding `qemu-system-riscv64` AND `qemu-system-riscv32` (this repo no longer builds QEMU). |
| `VSIM_BIN_DIR`      | External prebuilt vsim build dir holding the `sim_*` binaries (this repo no longer builds vsim; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning it). |

How it propagates:

- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
  the variable is missing.
- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives
  `NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`.

Override per-invocation without editing the file:

```sh
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain make -C tests/fixtures
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain ./andesim run \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>  # see docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md
```

### 1.4 Build everything

One command builds all three artifacts and exports the env vars the
test harness expects:

```sh
source ./setup.sh
```

`source` (not `bash`) is required so the script can prepend the build
dirs to PATH and export `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `VSIM_BIN_DIR`,
`QEMU_BIN_DIR`, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` into the current shell. The steps it
runs:

```
0/3 config     -> auto-copy config.env.example -> config.env (first run);
                  source it; export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN + QEMU_BIN_DIR + VSIM_BIN_DIR
1/3 QEMU       -> located (external prebuilt): $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64
2/3 vsim       -> located (external prebuilt): $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*
3/3 plugin     -> qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
```

Neither QEMU nor vsim is built here: build each in its own checkout and point
`QEMU_BIN_DIR` / `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (in `config.env`) at the dirs holding
`qemu-system-riscv64` / the `sim_*` binaries.

To rebuild the one component this repo still builds:

```sh
make -C qemu_plugin            # plugins; vendored qemu-plugin.h, no QEMU source needed
```

(vsim is rebuilt in your external vsim checkout via its own `build_vsim.sh`.)

To clean:

```sh
source ./setup.sh clean         # both
source ./setup.sh clean vsim
source ./setup.sh clean plugin
```

### 1.5 Build the test fixtures (RISC-V ELFs)

Fixtures are small RISC-V programs that exercise specific transport
paths. They are NOT built by `setup.sh`; build them once:

```sh
make -C tests/fixtures -j
```

One fixture at a time:

```sh
make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

Output ELFs land next to the sources under
`tests/fixtures/*.elf`. The fixtures depend on the Andes
RISC-V GCC (newlib); all C fixtures link through the vplat runtime
(section 5), so no semihosting library is involved. The toolchain path
comes from `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` (see section 1.3); to override for one
invocation:

```sh
make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain
```

### 1.6 Sanity check the build

```sh
# Artifacts present? (QEMU is external -- set via QEMU_BIN_DIR)
ls "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_ax45mpv_premium
ls qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so

# Smallest possible end-to-end - one marker-mode handoff:
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=marker TIMEOUT=120 \
  bash tests/e2e.sh
```

Expected last line:

```
[rt_c_v_matmul PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)
```

If you see `skip: ... not built`, redo `source ./setup.sh` and
re-build fixtures (`make -C tests/fixtures`).

# Out-of-tree build for the QEMU TCG plugin libhybrid_handoff.so. Standalone
# from the vsim CMake build because the plugin links against QEMU's plugin
# API + glib. Plugin sources live here and build here -- never inside the
# QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugin builds
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make
#   make clean
#
# Output: libhybrid_handoff.so in this directory.

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build vsim + plugin (qemu is external, prebuilt), then add the
# build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* directory) comes from
  # config.env -- this project integrates a prebuilt QEMU, it no longer builds one.
  VSIM_BIN_DIR="$ROOT/verilator/build"
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "cleaning vsim build ($VSIM_BIN_DIR)";   rm -rf "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "vsim cleaned"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64" ]; then
    err "no qemu-system-riscv64 under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64 (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 building vsim"
  "$ROOT/scripts/build_vsim.sh"
  ok "vsim -> $VSIM_BIN_DIR/vsim"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # The plugin builds against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h --
  # no QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_PLUGIN for e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC
